old_body:
Learn the language of the Quran so you can understand verses, duas and classical texts directly. The course covers vocabulary, grammar (Nahw and Sarf), pronunciation and conversation, with Quranic verses woven into every lesson.

Who is it for?

All levels. Absolute beginners start with the alphabet and pronunciation; intermediate learners move straight to grammar and syntax.

Materials

Free PDF worksheets, vocabulary lists and grammar guides — used in class and kept for revision at home.

How long until I understand verses?

With three classes a week, most students understand simple Quranic vocabulary and sentence structures within three to six months.

old_body:
Learn the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from verified collections such as Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim and Riyad as-Salihin — with translation, historical context and practical lessons for daily life.

For younger learners the course covers the essentials of practice: the steps of Wudu and Salah, daily duas, stories of the Prophets and Islamic manners.

Who is it for?

Children, teens and adults. No advanced Arabic is needed — concepts are built step by step in English.

old_body:
Our Hifz programme combines traditional recitation methods, proven memorisation techniques and a disciplined revision system. Each student follows a personal plan — the whole Quran, a particular Juz, or selected surahs.

Who is it for?

Children and adults who have completed Noorani Qaida (or equivalent) and can read Arabic correctly with basic Tajweed. You do not need to speak Arabic. Beginners should start with Noorani Qaida or Nazara first.

The three-part revision system

  • Sabaq — the new lesson, recited daily.
  • Sabqi — revision of the last seven days of memorisation.
  • Manzil — a steady rotation through everything memorised earlier.

Routine oral assessments keep memorisation strong and accurate.

How long does it take?

Memorising the whole Quran typically takes two to four years, depending on ability, class frequency and revision at home.

old_body:
Noorani Qaida is the classic foundation for reading the Quran. Your teacher starts with the Arabic letters and their correct articulation points (makharij), then builds step by step to joined letters, vowels, long vowels and the first Tajweed rules — until you can read complete verses with confidence.

Who is it for?

Complete beginners with no Arabic background: children from about 4½–5 years old, and adults who want to learn to read from scratch or correct their pronunciation.

How classes work

Every lesson is live and one-to-one. No physical book is needed — your teacher shows a digital Qaida on screen, and PDF copies are shared for practice at home. Female and male teachers are available.

How long does it take?

Children taking three classes a week usually finish in about four to six months. Adults often progress faster, depending on practice time.

old_body:
Our Nazara course takes you from careful reading to fluent, beautiful recitation. Lessons focus on accurate pronunciation, the essential rules of Tajweed and steady rhythm and breath control, with a growing understanding of what you are reciting.

Who is it for?

Children and adults who can recognise the Arabic letters and want to recite correctly — whether you are just starting to read the Quran or polishing your recitation. Sisters and young children can ask for a female teacher.

How classes work

Private live classes with video, screen-sharing and an interactive whiteboard. The pace adapts to each learner, and classes can be scheduled at any time of day.

old_body:
Designed for English speakers with little or no Arabic, this course explains the meaning of the Quran verse by verse — with context, clear explanation and discussion of how each lesson applies to everyday life.

Sources

Classes draw on established translations such as Sahih International, The Clear Quran by Dr Mustafa Khattab and Pickthall, together with classical Tafseer from Ibn Kathir.

How long does it take?

An overview of the key messages and chapters takes about six to twelve months. A detailed verse-by-verse Tafseer takes longer and is paced to suit you.
